title: Regularity of a ring map is local on the target
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ be a ring map of commutative rings with $\Lambda$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ with $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ write $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, for the induced map of localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The following are equivalent: (1) $\varphi$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; (2) $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; (3) $\varphi_{\mathfrak m'}:R_{\mathfrak m}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak m'}$ is regular for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'\subset\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$ (a prime ideal of $R$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local, line 10390); its proof cites Algebra Definition 00OD (regular ring: all local rings regular) and Algebra Lemma 00HT (lemma-flat-localization)

proof.text: Flatness of a ring map is equivalent to flatness of all induced maps on localizations at primes of the target, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion]. In the forward direction these local maps are the maps $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of the statement; in the reverse direction the local criterion reconstructs flatness of $\varphi$ from the assumed regular local maps.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), the local flatness criterion used in More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C0

proof.text: Assume $\varphi$ is flat. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ over $\mathfrak p\subset R$, localization identifies the fibre of $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ over $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ with the localization at $\mathfrak q$ of the fibre $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; the same holds after any finite purely inseparable extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Thus the fibre of $\varphi$ is geometrically regular exactly when all corresponding local fibres are regular local. The equivalence between a Noetherian ring being regular and all its localizations at primes being regular local is [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-local-criterion]. Therefore $\varphi$ is regular exactly when every $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local), proof: regularity of a Noetherian ring is checked on all local rings, together with the localization description of fibres from Definition Tag 07BZ

proof.text: The prime-local condition implies the maximal-local condition by localizing once more from a prime of $\Lambda$ to a maximal ideal containing it. Conversely, every prime $\mathfrak q$ of the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ is contained in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$, and regularity is local on the target by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-local-criterion]. Hence (1), (2), and (3) are equivalent.
